prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity visual-direction comp for a native iOS rail app
Primary request: Design a complete portrait iPhone first-screen UI for Last Train, an after-dark one-handed app for knowing the final direct departure and first train back.
Scene/backdrop: full-bleed 393x852-style app screen only, no phone hardware frame, no marketing poster, no environment outside the UI.
Exact visible content: "LAST TRAIN", "FAST TRAIN", "Upminster", "EAST", "23:47", "Shoeburyness", "22:58", "23:18", "23:32", "FIRST BACK", "05:12", "Direct services only".
Information hierarchy: station and direction scope first; one enormous primary last-train time 23:47; three compact earlier departures; first-back answer; mode switch is present but quiet. No journey durations. No +1 or calendar-next-day labels.
Visual world: cathode numeral stacks behind fine bronze anode gauze. Deep ink-blue black plane runs past every edge. Every possible departure numeral exists as a faint dark ghost; the current answer strikes forward crisp and glowing. Use bronze wire mesh, deep smoked glass, precise micro-grid, warm cathode orange for ordinary active information, bone-white body text, and #FF304C reserved only for the last train state. Ghost values may overlap in depth but all real UI text must remain readable.
Composition: no generic cards, no rounded glass dashboard, no bottom tab bar, no ornamental illustrations. Monumental 23:47 fills the upper half while a restrained rail-service stack remains below. Clean Dynamic Island safe area. Production-grade native iOS interface with clear touch affordances and readable typography.
Constraints: rail context must be unmistakable; red must only mean last train; output must look like a shipped operating screen rather than concept art; preserve exact text as closely as possible; no watermark.
